subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Japanese vs. Chinese Green Tea
description: One-minute skill: Japanese vs. Chinese Green Tea.

hook.text: Japanese and Chinese green teas taste nothing alike—even though they're the same type of tea.

buildup.text: Chinese green tea is pan-fired in a wok to stop oxidation. This gives it a toasty, nutty character.

discovery.text: Japanese green tea is steamed instead. Steaming preserves a vivid green color and a grassy, marine flavor.

twist.text: The difference is just seconds of heat applied differently. The same leaf, two techniques, two worlds of flavor.

climax.text: Chinese Longjing and Japanese Sencha are both green teas, but they'd fool anyone into thinking otherwise.

punchline.text: Pan-fired vs. steamed. One choice, two entirely different teas.

quiz.question: How do Japanese and Chinese green teas differ in processing?
options: Japan steams; China pan-fires the leaves
